Player Terrain
Use this list to place Terrain relative to this Player's starting location.
There are three ways that Terrain can be placed.
Terrain that is created outside of this mod is placed first.
Terrain created by any Player Terrain list (such as this one) is placed second.
Terrain created by the Map Terrain list (located in the Map Bonus panel) is placed third.
Caution should be used when changing terrain as it can lead to serious problems.
Here are some examples...
Creating a ring of mountains around a starting point will permanently isolate the player.
Creating a small island around the AI's starting location could cause it to end up being landlocked.
Terrain Controls
Use the Terrain controls located below to add commands to this list.
Each command will attempt to change the Terrain on one or more tiles when the map is created.
Please remember that each command adds to the total time required to create the map.
Terrain Menu
This menu contains a list of Terrain Types that can be added to the map.
Use this menu to select the current Terrain.
The current Terrain will appear in the image to the left.
Change Water/Land
Normally this mod does not change water tiles to land tiles and vice versa.
If this box is checked then water and land Terrain can be changed from one to the other.
Place
This determines how the mod will search for a suitable tile when changing Terrain.
Near causes the search to start at Minimum Distance and work its way out to Maximum Distance.
Far causes the search to start at Maximum Distance and work its way in to Minimum Distance.
Random causes the search to look for random tiles between Minimum and Maximum Distance.
Fill changes as much Terrain between Minimum and Maximum Distance as possible.
Count
This is the number of Terrain changes that will be made (if possible).
Minimum Distance
Terrain will be changed no closer than this distance from the player's starting position.
The Minimum Distance can never be greater than the Maximum Distance.
Attempting to move this slider past the Maximum Distance will cause that slider to follow.
Maximum Distance
Terrain will be changed no further than this distance from the player's starting position.
The Maximum Distance can never be less than the Minimum Distance.
Attempting to move this slider past the Minimum Distance will cause that slider to follow.
Elevation
This allows you to determine the tile's elevation when Terrain is changed.
This option is disabled if the current Terrain has no elevation.
Add To List
This will add a new command to this list using the current Terrain control settings.
List Controls
Once a command has been added to this list it has several controls used for editing.
Click on the small x button to delete the command from the list.
Click on the round button to copy the command's settings down to the Terrain controls.
Click on a update button to copy the Terrain control settings to that command.

Player Wonders
Use this list to place Natural Wonders relative to this Player's starting location.
There are three ways that Natural Wonders can be placed.
Wonders that are created outside of this mod are placed first.
Wonders created by any Player Wonder list (such as this one) are placed second.
Wonders created by the Map Wonder list (located in the Map Bonus panel) are placed third.
There are other options for controlling Natural Wonders in the Map panel.
Wonders within unit sight range at the start of the game do not give happiness for being discovered.
Great Barrier Reef and Rock of Gibraltar are not part of this mod due to graphics problems.
They can still appear if they are created outside of this mod.
Wonder Controls
Use the Wonder controls located below to add commands to this list.
Each command will attempt to place one or more Natural Wonders when the map is created.
Most Natural Wonders have very specific requirements for placement.
Depending on map conditions you may end up with little or no Natural Wonders of a given type.
Please remember that each command adds to the total time required to create the map.

Player Units
Use this list to replace this player's starting Units.
When this list is empty this player only receives Units that where created outside of this mod.
When this list is used this player only receives Units that where created by this mod.
Units are only placed if a suitable tile is found within an acceptable range of the starting location.
Once the area around the player's starting location is filled no more units will be added.
Units are placed on the map in the same order as they appear in this list.
Some units such as Air Units, Caravans, and Cargo Ships are placed after the Civ acquires their first city.
Cargo Ships require that the first city be a coastal city.

When Non-Combat is checked only Non-Combat Units are shown in the Unit menu.
When Both is checked both Combat and Non-Combat Units are shown in the Unit menu.
